rationale: Give the 018 critic's audit step a 600s await timeout (migration 705, applied+recorded, snapshot first). The first after-leg critique run today (work item e543ba1f, orchestration 6cc3cd38) failed with __step_error {message: 'Request timed out (code: TIMEOUT)', failed_step: 'audit'} while the render-audit adapter's REAL response — contrast findings for 8 of 40 URLs, captures taken — arrived at 17:26:24.57Z, ~182s after orchestration creation (17:23:22.06Z) and ~2 seconds after the default await timeout fired. The vision step never ran and no report was produced; the work item still read 'complete' because its result holds the spawn record (the bugs-287 pattern). Mechanism, read in the code not inferred: seed 645's audit step config carries no timeout_seconds, so the awaited request gets DefaultRequestTimeout = 180s (datahelpers/timeout_helpers.go:18). config.timeout_seconds is the honoured lever end-to-end: ConvertStepTimeout (timeout_helpers.go:23) lifts it into step.Timeout before routing, and both awaited-request builders stamp TimeoutAt via getTimeout(step) (coordinator.go:2482 and 2617). The 08-26 'before' run passed because the sweep was quicker before the hero batch made every page image-heavy; the step is now a ~2s coin-flip against the default on every dispatch. 600s is ~3.3x the measured sweep; the 5-minute stuck-orchestration takeover does not apply (it guards StatusExecutingStep, not awaiting-responses — approval steps await 24h on the same machinery).

plan.summary: One migration, 705: jsonb_set workflow.steps.audit.config.timeout_seconds = 600 on design-critique-agent, snapshot first, preconditions refusing on duplicate rows or an outranking workflow-level timeout key, post-condition reading back 600 with the outranking key still absent.

plan.risks: A genuinely hung adapter now holds the orchestration for up to 600s instead of 180s before the retry/failure path runs — bounded, and only on this manually-dispatched agent's audit step. If the sweep ever exceeds 600s the same failure returns; the sweep cost scales with max_pages (capped at 8), not site size, so growth is bounded by capture weight per page.
